title: The strict torus-to-grid density inequality for monochromatic k-in-a-row
statement:
Let $D(k,\mathbb{Z}^2)$ and $D(k, (\mathbb{Z}/k\mathbb{Z})^2)$ denote the corresponding maximum avoiding densities on the integer grid and the discrete torus, respectively. **Torus-density conjecture.** For every $k\in 3\mathbb{N}$,

$$
D(k,(\mathbb{Z}/k\mathbb{Z})^2)<D(k,\mathbb{Z}^2).
$$

The source records the general inequality in the opposite direction, gives strictness at $k=3$, and reports computational evidence at $k=6$; the proposed strict inequality remains open.
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.12880

Status: **open** according to the source (as of June 2026). “For small values of $k$, the conjecture has been verified in several cases , while it remains open in general.”
source_name: Kuo-Han Ku, “Monochromatic k in a row”, arXiv:2606.12880 (2026).
